city_center.name: Santa Fe Plaza
city_center.landmark: Santa Fe Plaza (National Historic Landmark) with the Palace of the Governors on the north side; Sangre de Cristo Mountains on the eastern skyline
city_center.notes: the Plaza was developed as the terminus of the Santa Fe Trail, fronted by adobe buildings with porticoes; the Santa Fe Farmers Market at the Railyard is the gathering anchor. sources: Santa Fe Plaza (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Plaza; sah-archipedia.org); santafe.com Santa Fe style.

cultural_notes: Santa Fe style is a fusion of Pueblo, Spanish Colonial, and Territorial influences designed for high-desert living, codified in Santa Fe roughly 1908-1940 -- Pueblo-Spanish Revival plus Territorial Revival (source: santafe.com Santa Fe style; en.wikipedia.org Pueblo Revival architecture; santafenm.gov design standards)

the Santa Fe Plaza is a National Historic Landmark in the style of traditional Spanish-American colonial cities, developed as the terminus of the Santa Fe Trail (source: Santa Fe Plaza, en.wikipedia.org; sah-archipedia.org)
'red or green?' is the official New Mexico state question; Santa Fe cuisine leans on both New Mexico chile and pinon (source: newmexico.org, shared with the Albuquerque record)

Northern Rio Grande Tewa Pueblos surround the city; Santa Fe is a major Native and Hispano arts market (Santa Fe Indian Market) -- tribal references stay consent-gated, no fabricated endorsement (INFERRED civic-culture framing; verify tone + honor sovereignty)
